html:
In spring 2010 the volcano under the Eyjafjallajökull glacier in southern Iceland erupted. Its ash cloud closed much of European airspace for about six days in April.

The eruption under ice produced fine, glassy ash, which winds carried towards Europe. Fearing damage to jet engines, governments grounded flights. About 100,000 flights were cancelled and millions of passengers stranded, the largest shutdown of air travel since the Second World War.

No one in Iceland was killed, though farms near the volcano were covered in ash. The event led to new rules on flying near ash. The world learned to stumble over the name, and the publicity helped start a tourism boom that lifted Iceland out of its financial crisis. Compare the far deadlier Laki eruption of 1783.
sum: In spring 2010 the volcano under the Eyjafjallajökull glacier in southern Iceland erupted. Its ash cloud closed much of European airspace for about six days in April.
